name: Ga'anda
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress
sweep_summary: Ga'anda (gaan1243) is not in the catalog. the list of works with stress in the title had one item, Newman 1977 'Y-prosody as a morphological process in Ga'anda'. The whole 1977 Leiden colloquium volume is open access at hdl.handle.net/1887/468 (Leiden University repository); automated download with a default UA is blocked by Leiden's protection page but a Chrome UA downloads the 22.8 MB image-only PDF, with. Pages 121-130 (PDF 133-142) were scanned at 250 dpi. The paper is a false positive for word stress: 'Y-prosody' is Firthian prosodic-analysis terminology for a morphologically conditioned palatalization feature (central vowels fronted, s > sh, final velar nasal > y) marking noun modified stems and 2nd/3rd-sg verb forms. Its only suprasegmental statement is footnote 5 (p. 121): 'Ga'anda has a three-tone system plus downstep (see R. Newman 1971b)'; stress/accent never occur in the text. No first-hand word-stress statement for Ga'anda was found. Remaining leads: Newman 1971b 'Downstep in Ga'anda' (JAL 10, tone; no online record found via OpenAlex/Crossref) and the 1971 UCLA dissertation (HathiTrust search-only; the only full grammar, medium priority for any phonology-chapter remark on stress).org, OpenAlex, Crossref and Wikipedia (the Wikipedia Ga'anda page has no phonology section).

sources.citation: Gravina, Richard (2014). The phonology of Proto-Central Chadic: the reconstruction of the phonology and lexicon of Proto-Central Chadic, and the linguistic history of the Central Chadic languages. LOT 375 (Leiden PhD).
sources.note: Mentions Ga'anda only four times, for classification (Tera group). States explicitly that the reconstruction does not include tone or stress; no Ga'anda-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Newman, Roxana Ma (1977). Y-prosody as a morphological process in Ga'anda. In Paul Newman & Roxana Ma Newman (eds.), Papers in Chadic Linguistics: papers from the Leiden Colloquium on the Chadic Language Family (Leiden, 15-17 September 1976), 121-130. Leiden: Afrika-Studiecentrum (Research reports 4).
sources.quote: SGa'anda has a three-tone system plus downstep (see R. Newman 1971b). Downstep occurs when a Hi tone is preceded by a non-segmental Mid or Lo tone (indicated by ' or ' written over a consonant, hyphen, or space). [fn. 5, p. 121] ... The overriding feature shared by these changes is palatality or "Y-coloration", functioning in the morphology as "Y-prosody". It is viewed as a prosodic feature because it applies to the entire noun stem, affecting all relevant segments within this domain. [p. 126] ... They involve primarily fronting of certain vowels and palatalization of certain consonants. [p. 121]
sources.locator: pp. 121 (opening paragraph and footnote 5), 126-127 (definition of Y-prosody), 130 (conclusion)
sources.note: Nothing. 'Prosody' here is Firthian: Y-prosody is a stem-wide palatalization feature (central vowels fronted, s > sh, stem-final velar nasal > y) that marks the modified stem of Y-class nouns and 2nd/3rd-sg-subject verb forms, and is morphologically not phonologically conditioned. The only suprasegmental statement in the paper is footnote 5: Ga'anda has a three-tone system plus downstep (citing R. Newman 1971b). The words stress/accent/prominence do not occur anywhere in the scanned paper (checked with fuzzy a full-text search for stress/accent). The scanned of tone marks is unreliable but th…
No phonology section at all; lists dialects Ga'anda, Gabin (Gabun), Fartata, cites Ethnologue, Blench 2006/2019 and Newman 1971. Nothing on stress or tone.

sources.note: Bibliographic records only. Glottolog lists nine references for Ga'anda; the only descriptive one (listed by Glottolog as a grammar) is Newman 1971a. Meek 1931, Boyle 1915, Kraft 1981 and Jungraithmayr & Ibriszimow 1994 are wordlist/comparative works; Glottolog gives no phonology-type reference for the language.

sources.citation: WALS Online (Dryer & Haspelmath eds.), language Ga'anda (wals code gnd), CLDF from github.com/cldf-datasets/wals
sources.note: Ga'anda is coded for 13 WALS features, all morphosyntactic (33A, 37A, 38A, 83A, 85A-88A, 90A, 90C, 95A-97A), every one sourced to Newman 1971 with page numbers; it is NOT coded for 13A Tone, 14A Fixed Stress Locations or 15A weight-sensitive Stress. WALS therefore has no stress information for Ga'anda.
